chunks: What al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said:

A companion of ours went to ask Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a woman who dies among men, among whom there is no mahram. Should they perform ghusl for her while her clothes are on her? He said: Then that would lead them into that matter; rather, they should wash her two hands.

key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the deceased woman being asked about in the ruling
key_terms.ثِيَابُهَا: her garments, mentioned as remaining on her body
key_terms.ذُو مَحْرَمٍ: a man of unmarriageable kinship whose presence affects the burial ruling
key_terms.كَفَّيْهَا: her two hands, the only part instructed to be washed
key_terms.يُغَسِّلُونَهَا: they perform ritual washing of the deceased upon her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman dies among unrelated men with no mahram present to wash her?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling regarding the death of a woman in the presence of unrelated men when no mahram is present. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام forbids full washing in such a case due to the impropriety involved, and instead instructs that only her hands be washed.
